## The one-liner

> We integrated **yfinance close prices** into **specific portfolios** so that
> **investors and traders** can **assume the appropriate risk for investment strategy**.

**Role:** I developed core strategic directions, created portfolio structures, and 
**Team:** Dane Herrin and Alexander Jackson
**Repo:** [https://github.com/DaneHerrin/data510--Quant-Back-Testing-](https://github.com/DaneHerrin/data510--Quant-Back-Testing-)

## The question

This project is designed for stakeholders who need to evaluate portfolio risk beyond simple return. We focus on risk adjusted return for stakeholders that don't need high speed growth, but stable, long-term gains. This is namely institutional funds and risk-averse investors. This strategy can be partially used in conjunction with riskier investments, such as VC or other high-volatility funds and unstable returns. 

## The data

We used historical daily market data from Yahoo Finance accessed through the `yfinance` python package.

## The approach

We combine backtesting, risk analysis, and statistical time-series modeling. We created several different sector representative portfolios covering energy, commercial real estate, tech, and FMCG, as well as a barbell strategy that combines fixed income securities with VIX options. We factor the risk for each portfolio using Sharpe and Sortino ratios over different drawdown and recovery periods. We then looked at the results, determining which portfolios performed better according to different criteria.
